title: Rational geometric fibres dominate modifications of a nodal trait curve
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $F$, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C\to T$ be H-projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Suppose every singularity of a geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $C$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and normal, meaning that all its local rings are integrally closed domains. For every integral $\Gamma$ with an H-projective morphism $p:\Gamma\to C$ whose restriction over $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is an isomorphism, there are an integral scheme $Y$, an H-projective morphism $h:Y\to C$ also an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}F$, and a proper surjective $C$-morphism $a:Y\to\Gamma$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], with $pa=h$, having the following property: for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$, the reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of the geometric fibre $Y\times_C\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is either a point or a nonempty connected union of finitely many irreducible components, each isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ [def-sc-p1-standard].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-generic-nodal-trait-normality] to $C$: every local ring is an integrally closed domain, and $C$ is integral as $C_F$ is. By [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] $C$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-regularization] to obtain a finite tower $r:Z\to C$ of blowups of reduced nonregular closed special-fibre points, with $Z$ regular, all stages flat finitely presented nodal families, and $r$ an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}F$. On each stage (generic fibre $C_F$) the normality lemma gives integrality and [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] Noetherianity, local dimensions at most two, and dimension two at closed special-fibre points. Each arrow is H-projective by [lem-sfb-projective-affine-base-blowup] ($A$ and the stages are Noetherian); [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] makes $r$ H-projective.

Apply [lem-sfb-regular-trait-modification-graph-tower] to $r$ and the given $p$: $C$ is integral H-projective over $T$ with nonempty integral generic fibre, and $Z$ satisfies its hypotheses by Step 1. Obtain a tower $Y\to Z$ of blowups of reduced closed special-fibre points with regular two-dimensional local rings, and $a:Y\to\Gamma$ with $pa=h=rb_1\cdots b_m$. Here $Y$ is integral, and $h$ is H-projective and an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Tag 0C5H (lemma-extend-rational-map-blowing-up), whose proof is the reduced graph plus Tag 0AHI (lemma-dominate-by-blowing-up-in-points); returned Steps 4--6

proof.text: Concatenate the two towers over $X_0=C$; all stages are integral Noetherian by Steps 1--2. The nodal centres satisfy (a) of [lem-sfb-trait-point-tower-rational-components] by Step 1 (whole stage nodal, nonregular at the centre), the later ones (b) by Step 2. Thus every reduced geometric fibre of $h$ has dimension at most one and finitely many components, and each positive-dimensional component is $\mathbf P^1$ over its specified geometric field.

Since $pa=h$, $a$ is a $C$-morphism. The source $Y$ is proper over $C$ by [lem-pc-projective-proper], and $\Gamma$ is separated over $C$ because $p$ is projective. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $a$ proper. Over $\operatorname{Spec}F$, $a$ is the isomorphism $p_F^{-1}h_F$, so its closed image contains the nonempty, hence dense, generic fibre of the integral $\Gamma$; hence $a$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 01W6, proper source to separated target; closed image containing a dense open

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-normal-geometric-connectedness] to $h$, proper by Step 4. Its source is integral, hence reduced, with generic point in $Y_F\cong C_F$, mapping to the generic point $\xi$ of $C$; its target is integral normal (Step 1); its fibre over $\xi$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$, with global functions $\kappa(\xi)$. Hence every geometric fibre is nonempty connected, and so is its reduction. If it has dimension zero, it is one point (finitely many components, Step 3) whose reduced local ring is a field; [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] makes it $\Omega$. Otherwise a zero-dimensional component would be a closed point in no other component, hence open and closed in the finite union, contradicting connectedness. So all components are one-dimensional and Step 3 identifies them with $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$.
